case: A failure record stops moving without recording whether its error class is terminal.
why: `no_progress` is not a lifecycle PHASE -- the phases are observed, investigating, retry_admitted, blocked, resolved -- so "terminal" has no registered meaning unless the record says so. With the flag no longer demanded, a record reaches `blocked` and nothing on it distinguishes a failure that stopped from one that is still being worked, which is the condition under which the payload conditional never has to bind. Coverage note: F6C-16 measured 14 of 30 guards with a paired fixture, and every guard this amendment adds is owed one.
